title: Investigate API key aliasing causing delayed usage attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Symptom: Multiple customers have reported transient throttling and mis-billed usage after rotating API keys. Investigation shows that for some key rotation sequences the platform attributed traffic to the previous tenant for up to several hours, which caused incorrect quota enforcement and spike in support tickets.

Repro steps observed: 
1) Customer creates a new API key (rotate operation that writes alias records).
2) Client continues to use the old key during a short window while the new key is being distributed (edge caches may see either key).
3) Our rate-limiter cell consults its local key->tenant cache and sometimes resolves the old alias to the previous owner because the alias-update message was delayed or applied out-of-order across cells.
4) Requests are counted against (or limited by) the wrong tenant until caches converge.

Hypothesis: Race between alias-update propagation and per-cell in-memory key-owner caches (and a missing version/epoch check) + write ordering inconsistency in the alias service. Secondary contributor: our usage attribution pipeline materializes owner mapping asynchronously and backfills counts, so real-time enforcement can diverge.

Impact: Customer-facing throttles, misattributed billing spikes for both donor and recipient tenants, and elevated support load. Occurs on multi-key rotations and when rotational traffic patterns are high (burst windows).

Goal: Implement a safe fix to ensure deterministic, near-real-time owner mapping after key operations and to reduce blast radius while preserving throughput. Provide mitigations for already-impacted windows and postmortem.
comments: 2025-09-16 - Raj P.: Confirmed reproducer script that simulates staggered key rotations across two cells. Repro succeeds ~70% in local multi-cell env. Collected traces from rate-limiter: missing alias epoch header in 40% of requests.

2025-09-17 - Priya S. (SRE): Saw alias-update message lag on Kafka partition 3 during rotation events; consumer lag correlated with partitions undergoing GC. Filed follow-up to tune consumer configs (ENG-25390).

2025-09-18 - Raj P.: Small PoC: attach a monotonic alias-epoch header to alias-update events; rate-limiter rejects stale epochs. PoC reduces misattribution in test harness to <1% but increases per-request checks — need perf run.

2025-09-20 - Design review with runtime team: two approaches debated: (A) strong consistency via a synchronous key-lookup call to alias service on cold-miss (impact: added p95 latency), (B) optimistic local cache with epoch validation and short blocking refresh on epoch mismatch (preferred).

2025-09-22 - Raj P.: Created branch and PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/ENG-25346 (WIP). Implemented alias-epoch header and cache validation with background refresh. Running perf tests: baseline token-processing throughput drop ~3% under synthetic load.

2025-09-24 - QA: Added chaos tests to simulate partition lags; behavior improved but observed a rare case where simultaneous double-rotate (two quick successive rotates) can still cause transient attribution flip-flop. Need additional write-order guard or tombstone semantics.

2025-09-26 - Maya C. (PM): Customer Impact log linked: confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/ENG-25346-Customer-Impact. Agreed to customer communication draft and temporary quota grace for impacted orgs while fix rolls out.

2025-09-28 - Raj P.: Rollout plan ready. Canary to 5% of runtime cells with extended telemetry. Post-rollout migration script to reconcile any misattributed usage for last 48 hours. Filing migration job ENG-25347.
